articles.title: ‘SNL’ caregiving sketch gives new momentum to bipartisan push in Congress
articles.summary: A legislative push to support people who provide out-of-pocket care for their aging parents got a boost from a viral “Saturday Night Live” (“SNL”) sketch that sparked renewed conversation about the reality of gender disparities in unpaid caregiving networks. The comedy sketch “Sister” drew laughter when it aired Nov. 14, but its truth has…
articles.body:
A legislative push to support people who provide out-of-pocket care for their aging parents got a boost from a viral “Saturday Night Live” (“SNL”) sketch that sparked renewed conversation about the reality of gender disparities in unpaid caregiving networks.

The comedy sketch “Sister” drew laughter when it aired Nov. 14, but its truth has reverberated online among people living the everyday realities of providing unpaid long-term care.

In the sketch, which has amassed more than 9 million views on YouTube, comedian John Mulaney plays a son who is seeking an alternative to an expensive live-in caregiver for his aging father. The answer? His sister, who will drop everything to come care for their dad without his help.

Blaire Bryant, the vice president of the National Alliance for Caregiving, said the sketch hit home for her.

“I really resonated with it because I am the sister too,” she said. “It really makes you reflect on the fact that this is a common experience, a shared experience.”

Anne Hubbard, the chief public policy officer for the American Parkinson Disease Association, said the sketch “struck a chord” for many women serving as caregivers across the country.

“There’s never been anything so popularized as that skit that just you know really hits the nail on the head with you know the existing situation that many women find themselves in,” she said. “They’re taking care of their children, they’re taking care of aging parents, and managing that balancing act all while potentially also holding down a career is a significant challenge.”

A KFF poll released last week found that women were more likely than men to report being caregivers at 32 percent compared with 26 percent of men. Around 6 in 10 of all caregivers are women.

Women also take on a larger share of the emotional and physical toll of caregiving, with men reporting similar negative impacts on finances to women in these caregiving roles, according to the KFF survey.

Shannon Schumacher, a senior survey analyst for the public opinion and survey research program at KFF, noted that data indicates people across all demographics report experiencing strains tied to their unpaid caregiving duties.

“Across a lot of these measures, we do see some differences where women are more likely to spend time providing care and are doing slightly different types of care,” Schumacher said.

The renewed conversation around caregiving comes amid an effort to pass the bipartisan Lowering Costs for Caregivers Act, which would allow family caregivers to use tax-free flexible spending or health savings accounts to cover a parent’s medical costs.

The National Alliance for Caregiving and the American Parkinson Disease Association were among the more than 100 organizations to sign on to a letter led by the Families and Caregivers Economic Security (FACES) Coalition last week, calling on Congress to take up the bill.

FACES Coalition leader Catherine Finley called the legislation a “first step” to providing relief for unpaid caregivers.

“It’s not going to change the world for a caregiver, but every little bit is really meaningful,” she said. “From the coalition’s perspective, we’d like to see Congress take that first step and get something done to recognize the financial toll on caregivers, and then we build from there.”

Adult caregivers spend an average of about $11,500 per year, or an average of 31 percent of annual household income, on caregiving costs, according to the AARP’s 2026 Caregiving Out-of-Pocket Costs study.

Megan O’Reilly, AARP’s vice president of government affairs, called the Lowering Costs for Caregivers Act “common sense” and cited the “strong bipartisan bicameral support” it has received in Congress.

“Years ago, you had to talk to someone about what is a family caregiver. Today, we don’t have to do that,” she said. “I think we’ve made tremendous progress in elevating the issue and the sort of challenges and sort of the sense of urgency, and so I think … we’re at the time to deliver relief for caregivers.”

O’Reilly said she hopes Congress will focus on strengthening support for long-term care systems in the U.S. and expanding Medicare coverage for hearing, dental and vision services — priorities Democrats have outlined for when they take power next year.

Bryant, of the National Alliance for Caregiving, said there is “much, much more policy” needed to strengthen the nation’s long-term care system, including proposed Medicare reforms.

“It also starts with recognizing that caregivers, many caregivers, are still also working, so how do we build out support through the workforce to better support that ability to work and care at the same time?” Bryant said.

“The Lowering Cost for Caregivers Act puts money in the pockets of caregivers, but we have an additional ecosystem of supports that need to happen and reforms that need to happen to better support family caregivers.”

articles.title: From turkey shortages to helicopter deliveries: The extraordinary history of Thanksgiving during war
articles.summary: The U.S. military has delivered Thanksgiving dinner to troops from Civil War Union troops to Vietnam's War Zone D, a tradition born in wartime.
articles.body: In November 1966, 12 American soldiers stationed at an isolated outpost in a Vietnamese war zone were about as far from a traditional Thanksgiving at home as they could get. Their only means of resupply was by air. But the U.S. military was determined to get them Thanksgiving dinner anyway. A mess sergeant at Bien Hoa prepared turkey and all the trimmings, packed the meal into insulated containers and sent it by helicopter into War Zone D, where three officers and nine enlisted men of a 5th Special Forces detachment sat down to Thanksgiving dinner, according to Defense Department records preserved by the National Archives. The delivery was one piece of a massive logistical effort the U.S. military has undertaken during wars spanning generations to get traditional Thanksgiving meals to troops serving in combat zones. From civilians sending tens of thousands of turkeys to Union troops during the Civil War to helicopters carrying hot meals to soldiers in Korea, the holiday has been observed through some of the nation's most consequential conflicts. Thanksgiving became a national tradition in the midst of war. President Abraham Lincoln issued his 1863 Thanksgiving proclamation as the Civil War entered its third year, calling on Americans to observe the final Thursday of November as a day of "Thanksgiving and Praise." By the following year, Americans on the home front were mounting a massive effort to get Thanksgiving dinner to Union troops. Former War Department official Charles A. Dana later recalled the "great turkey movement" of November 1864. In New York alone, organizers reported having 20,000 turkeys ready to send to the front, according to Dana's account. A Philadelphia committee sought transportation for another 4,000 destined for troops serving under Gen. Philip Sheridan. By World War II, the effort to put turkey on troops' Thanksgiving tables had grown so large that it affected whether Americans at home could find one for their own. In August 1943, the War Food Administration restricted most civilian turkey sales as the government sought millions of pounds for the armed forces. An initial goal of at least 10 million pounds for troops overseas was expanded to include military installations at home, and the government ultimately obtained roughly 30 million pounds before the order was lifted in October, according to wartime government records. A year later, delivering Thanksgiving dinner near the front could carry its own risks. 102-YEAR-OLD NAVY VETERAN STILL CRAVES HOT WINGS AFTER 102 COMBAT MISSIONS IN KOREA: 'I MIGHT MAKE IT TO 115' In Germany's Hürtgen Forest, Lt. Paul Boesch of the 121st Infantry Regiment later recalled being told that hot turkey dinners had arrived for his men amid some of the European campaign's most grueling fighting. Boesch protested that sending soldiers to collect the food would expose them to German artillery, but the order to distribute the meal stood. His fears proved well-founded. As troops gathered to retrieve the food, German artillery struck the area, killing and wounding several men, according to Boesch's account. Six years later, American troops were again eating Thanksgiving dinner near the front, this time in the bitter cold of North Korea. On Thanksgiving Day 1950, Marines around the Chosin Reservoir were served turkey and cranberry sauce, candied sweet potatoes, fruitcake and mince pie. In the subzero temperatures, the food quickly began to freeze. US NAVY RELEASES PHOTOS OF 'FRESH MEALS,' PUSHES BACK ON REPORTS OF FOOD SHORTAGES ON MIDDLE EAST WARSHIPS The dinner came as U.S. commanders remained optimistic that the war could soon be over. The following day, Gen. Douglas MacArthur launched an offensive that became known as the "Home-by-Christmas" campaign. Instead, Chinese forces entered the fighting in massive numbers. Within days of Thanksgiving, Marines around Chosin were surrounded and battling through one of the most brutal engagements of the Korean War. More than half a century later, another generation of American troops was spending Thanksgiving at war in Iraq and Afghanistan. In 2003, President George W. Bush secretly flew into Baghdad to surprise roughly 600 troops gathered for Thanksgiving dinner at Baghdad International Airport. Air Force One approached with its cabin shades drawn and lights dimmed amid tight security surrounding the trip. "I was just looking for a warm meal somewhere," Bush joked before addressing the troops and helping serve Thanksgiving dinner. In Afghanistan, getting that dinner to troops stationed far from major bases could require a different kind of operation. On Thanksgiving 2007, helicopters carried turkeys and traditional fixings from Bagram Airfield to soldiers at remote firebases in the Tagab Valley, according to a contemporaneous U.S. military account. It was the first hot meal some of the soldiers had eaten in months. Because the positions still had to be defended, troops rotated between Thanksgiving dinner and standing watch. "The white meat was magnificent," Pfc. Matt Lorimer of the 82nd Airborne Division said. At another remote Afghan outpost two years later, troops spent a month fattening five scrawny turkeys purchased locally for Thanksgiving. But five birds were not enough to feed roughly 150 soldiers. Additional turkey was flown from the United States to Bagram Airfield and then transported to the outpost. Even that was not the end of the journey. Their Thanksgiving dinner was packed up and flown by helicopter up the mountain to them.

articles.title: Employees at GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games reject union
articles.summary: Employees at Rockstar Games, the developer behind “Grand Theft Auto VI,” overwhelmingly voted against recognizing a union this week. In a Thursday vote, 75.3 percent of employees, or 1,163 team members, voted against recognizing the Rockstar Game Workers Union with the Independent Workers of Great Britain (IWGB), while 24.7 percent, or 381 members, voted in…
articles.body:
Employees at Rockstar Games, the developer behind “Grand Theft Auto VI,” overwhelmingly voted against recognizing a union this week.

In a Thursday vote, 75.3 percent of employees, or 1,163 team members, voted against recognizing the Rockstar Game Workers Union with the Independent Workers of Great Britain (IWGB), while 24.7 percent, or 381 members, voted in favor. The vote had a 93.2 percent turnout among Rockstar employees.

The vote meant the company wasn’t required to recognize the worker’s union or had any obligation to engage with collective bargaining negotiations.

IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union wrote in a statement, according to the BCC , that anyone who worked at the game company that “believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for.”

“Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues,” the organization continued. “We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.”

Jennifer Kolbe, Rockstar Game’s head of publishing, told The Hill that the company was “extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we’ve built together and the launch of ‘Grand Theft Auto VI.’”

“This result reflects our team’s strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong,” she added.

“As we look ahead, we’re excited to build on all we’ve accomplished together,” Kolbe concluded.

The union is currently representing 23 workers in an employment tribunal which finished hearing evidence on Nov. 18, just one day before “Grand Theft Auto VI” was released.

The failed vote comes after Rockstar employees alleged the company participated in wage discrimination practices based on gender. Game Developer reported in July that median wages between genders had allegedly widened ahead of the release of “Grand Theft Auto VI” as equal pay initiatives were scrapped at the company.

articles.title: NBC Pulls Ad Criticizing U.S. Military Aid to Israel After Backlash, Reviews Approval Process
articles.summary: The ad aired during Wednesday's 'SNL' Thanksgiving special without senior NBC management's knowledge, a source familiar with the situation tells The Hollywoo...
articles.body:
NBC will not air a controversial anti-Israel advertisement again after it drew backlash for airing during Wednesday night's Saturday Night Live Thanksgiving special.

A person familiar with the situation told The Hollywood Reporter that senior management was unaware of the advertisement until after it aired. NBCUniversal will now evaluate its advertising approval process to ensure appropriate levels of review.

The 30-second advertisement, titled "Every Three Seconds," shows a young girl saving money for a year by doing yard work, including mowing the lawn, blowing leaves and shoveling snow, until she raises $400 to buy a bicycle. The ad then cuts to a girl in Gaza, standing on crutches and missing a leg amid rubble, as the narrator draws a comparison between the two scenarios and U.S. military aid to Israel.

"Over a year, she saved $400 for a new bicycle," the voiceover says. It then cuts to the girl in Gaza. "Every three seconds, our government sends $400 of taxpayer money to Israel to do this."

The advertisement was paid for by the Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project, or IMEU Policy Project. This pro-Palestinian advocacy nonprofit supports ending U.S. military aid to Israel. The group's campaign, titled "No More for Israel," encourages viewers to contact their congressional representatives to oppose continued military assistance to the country.

After the advertisement aired, several Jewish and pro-Israel organizations criticized NBC for broadcasting the spot.

Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt criticized the network in a post on X, writing , "Again and again, why do people in positions of authority fail to demonstrate basic decency, let alone respect, for the Jewish community? At a moment of escalating antisemitism, there is no rationale to justify fanning the flames with such a twisted narrative."

B'nai B'rith International also condemned the advertisement in a Facebook post.

"Shame on NBC," the nonprofit wrote . "The suffering of innocent civilians is a tragedy. But using a child's pain to spread a twisted, one-sided story that blames the Jewish state, and by extension Jews everywhere, is disgusting."

Jim Berk, CEO of the Simon Wiesenthal Center, also shared a statement with THR criticizing the network for airing the advertisement.

"The advertisement's imagery, an American child's hardship set against the anguish of a child in Gaza, offers viewers a seductive but unsubstantiated narrative: that the struggles of American families are somehow bound up with U.S. support for Israel," the statement reads in part. "In collapsing a complex foreign policy into a single, emotionally charged imagery, erases the deeper realities, including the imperative to protect Israeli lives and the very existence of the country itself. By manipulating emotion and stripping it of context, this ad seeks to become a catalyst for hostility."

articles.title: 15 hospitalized in potential Thanksgiving food poisoning at Florida medical center
articles.summary: Fifteen people were hospitalized due to possible food poisoning from Leon Medical Center headquarters’ Thanksgiving event, according to Miami-Dade Fire Rescue officials. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue told a local NBC affiliate that crews responded to reports of potential food poisoning before the call was shifted to a Level 1 mass casualty incident. The agency continued that…
articles.body:
Fifteen people were hospitalized due to possible food poisoning from Leon Medical Center headquarters’ Thanksgiving event, according to Miami-Dade Fire Rescue officials.

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue told a local NBC affiliate that crews responded to reports of potential food poisoning before the call was shifted to a Level 1 mass casualty incident. The agency continued that it initiated medical treatment before 15 people were hospitalized.

The center is located in Doral, Fla., where local police told The Hill that Leon Medical Centers was hosting its annual Thanksgiving luncheon before attendees began showing signs consistent with possible illness. Doral Police stated the illness’s source remains unclear.

“Leon Medical Centers contracted an external caterer to provide a Thanksgiving luncheon for its staff at its Doral Headquarters,” the company wrote in a statement provided to CBS News . “Some of the staff began to experience gastrointestinal symptoms shortly after the luncheon and required treatment.”

“We continue to work with the caterers to determine, if possible, the cause and continue to provide support to our staff and their families,” the center said. “No patients are affected by this incident which was limited to the Company’s headquarters facility.”

“Please note that this did not occur at any of the Leon Medical Centers healthcare facilities,” it concluded.

Food poisoning occurs when people ingest certain germs – such as Salmonella or E. coli – which can cause a variety of mild to serious symptoms, according to the Centers for Disease Control (CDC). While some germs take days to cause illness, other germs can make individuals sick within a few hours.

Common symptoms include nausea, vomiting, stomach pains or cramps, diarrhea or having a fever.

The CDC recommends that individuals experiencing diarrhea or vomiting drink lots of water to avoid dehydration.

Miami-Dade Fire Rescue did not respond immediately to The Hill’s request for comment.

articles.title: Two American Airlines planes clip wings before takeoff at Reagan airport in 'tense' moment
articles.summary: No injuries were reported, and the FAA plans to investigate the incident, which occurred during taxiing.
articles.body:
Two American Airlines jets hit each other at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport while taxiing for departure in Washington DC on Friday.

One jet "clipped the wing" of the other at around 5:10 ET (22:10 GMT), the Federal Aviation Administration said in a statement. No injuries were reported, and the FAA plans to investigate.

Both aircraft returned to the gate and were removed from service to be inspected by maintenance teams, American Airlines said.

The incident happened at the same airport where 67 people died in a deadly collision between a jetliner and an Army helicopter in January 2025.

"American Airlines Flight 638 clipped the wing of American Airlines Flight 2152 while taxiing for departure," the FAA said.

Air traffic controllers can be heard on an audio recording saying two Boeing 737s clipped on the airport's runway. The controllers requested an emergency response and fire personnel to the plane, then directed the aircraft to return to the gate.

The "wingtips of both Boeing 737-800s made contact", American Airlines said in a statement. The airline added that it is working to get affected passengers who were evacuated from both planes to their destinations as soon as possible.

A passenger on flight 2152 headed to Chicago's O'Hare airport told the BBC that he felt a "large jolt" on the right side of the aircraft as they were taxiing before departure. The other plane, flight 638, was bound for Dallas-Fort Worth airport.

The passenger added that the "aircraft shook quite violently" upon impact and he heard gasps inside the cabin. He described the moment as "tense", but that nobody seemed to be hurt.

As he looked out the window, he saw a piece of the aircraft on the ground. It looked like the "tip of the wing", he said, describing how the other aircraft's wing was overlapping his plane's wing.

The BBC has contacted American Airlines about reports of the broken wingtip.

As they taxied back to the gate, the passenger said he saw a truck pick up the piece that had fallen.

The fact that this isn't the first incident at this airport was "definitely scary", the passenger said.

Last year, there was a deadly mid-air collision between another American Airlines flight and a military helicopter at Reagan National.

The 64 people on the passenger plane and three US Army members on the Black Hawk helicopter all died in the crash.

The aircraft, en route to land at the DC airport after leaving from Wichita, Kansas, was sent careening into the Potomac River upon impact with the military helicopter.

It was later determined that the helicopter was receiving faulty altitude data, causing it to fly higher than intended.

Reagan National Airport is the smaller of the two DC-area airports and caters mostly to domestic flights.

It sits right near the sprawl of the US capital, the White House and the Pentagon.

Earlier this week, the US Army said it planned to resume helicopter test flights near Reagan airport, according to CBS News, BBC's US News partner. The flights were paused following last year's incident.

BBC has contacted the Pentagon for comment.

articles.title: NCP (SP) MLA Awhad extends support for delimitation bill; Supriya says call hinges on draft
articles.summary: NCP (SP) signals support for delimitation bill but says final call awaits draft review; Supriya Sule skips INDIA meet as Sharad Pawar is hospitalized.
articles.body: PUNE: NCP (SP) MLA Jitendra Awhad on Friday said his party would support the delimitation bill, while Baramati MP Supriya Sule asserted that they would decide on it only after going through the draft though she would give the INDIA bloc meeting in Delhi on Saturday a miss as her father was in hospital.After meeting NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Breach Candy Hospital, Awhad told reporters in Mumbai that the decision to support the bill had been taken. “Things are very clear. It has been decided to support the delimitation bill,” he said.Awhad, a member of NCP (SP)’s core committee, said he had briefly discussed the delimitation issue with Pawar even before parleys on it began. “Pawar saheb had said delimitation was a constitutional process and had to be carried out,” he said.Supriya, in contrast, told TOIthat the party would decide whether to support the legislation or not only after examining its draft. Earlier in the day also, she told reporters in Mumbai, “You will know about the party’s line on the floor of Lok Sabha.”In a social media post, Supriya said she would travel to Delhi only on Monday and would remain in Mumbai till then because of Pawar’s hospitalisation. Thus, she would not attend the INDIA bloc meeting in Delhi on Saturday, where the proposed legislation was likely to figure prominently. Party MP and chief whip in Lok Sabha, Amol Kolhe, said NCP (SP) MP from Ahilyanagar district Nilesh Lanke would represent the party at the meeting.Kolhe issued a three-line whip on behalf of NCP (SP) to all its eight Lok Sabha MPs on Friday, directing them to remain present in the House from Nov 30 to Dec 3, stating that a “very important business would be taken up”. He told TOI that Awhad’s statement about NCP (SP) supporting the delimitation bill could have been based on reports that the party’s two demands raised publicly had been met.“These two or three points do not constitute the entire draft of the bill. Let the draft come, we will evaluate it. All eight MPs will sit together and take a call on whether to support it or not,” he said, adding that the reasons for supporting or opposing the legislation had to be clear before the party took a final decision.NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar on Friday appeared to have softened his stand on the delimitation bill. He said political positions should be taken only after the draft was made public rather than rejecting the proposal outright.After meeting his grandfather Pawar in the hospital, Rohit told reporters, “Once the draft is out, our MPs will go through it. We are hopeful that our party, particularly Supriya tai, will take an appropriate stand on this matter.”The Union cabinet on Friday approved the proposed legislation. According to sources, it provides for a 50% increase in the number of seats in each state. Sule had earlier said her party could back the bill if it provided for a uniform 50% increase in seats across all states and incorporated women’s reservation.Government has convened a four-day special session of Lok Sabha from Nov 30 to Dec 3 and a two-day sitting of Rajya Sabha on Dec 2 and 3. NCP (SP) has eight MPs in Lok Sabha and one in Rajya Sabha.A senior NCP (SP) member, speaking on condition of anonymity, said any political party opposing or supporting the bill must have a reason for it. “Samajwadi Party’s Akhilesh Yadav wants seats for each state based on population. NCP (SP) and DMK are opposed to it. Congress has not clarified the reason for its opposition,” he said.He said NCP (SP) had objected to three clauses when the bill was introduced last time, and all three had since been dropped. articles.title: Mamdani handed out $95K in staff raises the same day he warned of $12B budget deficit: report
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani approved $850,000 in raises for City Hall aides in his first year, according to payroll records reviewed by the New York Post.
articles.body: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani approved roughly $850,000 in pay raises for dozens of City Hall aides during his first year in office, according to municipal payroll records reviewed by the New York Post. The records show the raises were distributed to at least 46 staffers since Mamdani took office in January, bringing total compensation increases near $1 million. The Post counted 21 new hires who received raises totaling $450,000 before their first anniversary on the job, more than twice the combined number of first-year employees who got raises under Eric Adams and Bill de Blasio. MAMDANI TURNS ON NEW YORK CITY TEACHERS UNION WITH LAWSUIT BLOCKING PAY RAISES FOR EDUCATORS On Jan. 28, five City Hall employees were granted salary increases totaling $95,000 on the same day Mamdani announced New York City faced an estimated $12 billion budget deficit, the records show. The mayor’s office later lowered that projected deficit to approximately $5.4 billion. The mayor’s office on Nov. 12 confirmed the city’s fiscal 2027 budget rose $3.3 billion from the budget adopted in June, reaching $129.2 billion. MAMDANI'S TAXPAYER-FUNDED INFLUENCER ARMY ACCUSED OF PLOTTING PRESSURE CAMPAIGN AGAINST NYC CEOS The payroll disclosures detail significant salary adjustments across several executive staff positions. Julia Simcoe and Jacob Russell each received raises of more than $60,000, bringing their salaries to $148,000 and $145,000, respectively, the Post reported. Three other City Hall staffers received raises ranging from $30,000 to $45,000. MAMDANI’S AFFORDABILITY REVOLUTION STUMBLED AS RENT COSTS SOAR TO RECORD HIGHS The salary increases come as Mamdani, who took office Jan. 1 as the city's first self-described socialist mayor, faces fiscal constraints and administrative hurdles on core campaign pledges. Mamdani’s plan to eliminate bus fares across the five boroughs has stalled after pushback from New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, who noted the Metropolitan Transportation Authority cannot absorb the loss of revenue from fare boxes. While Mamdani’s campaign estimated the initiative would cost $700 million, the New York City Independent Budget Office (IBO) projected that fully eliminating fares would cost New York State roughly $1.1 billion. EXPERTS SCORCH MAMDANI'S GROCERY PLAN AS AN 'ILLUSION' THAT WILL HAVE TAXPAYERS FOOTING THE BILL The administration has also faced capacity limits with its universal childcare initiative. A pilot program aimed at 2-year-olds launched with 2,000 available seats but drew more than 5,700 applicants, leaving roughly 3,700 children on waitlists. The program cost $73 million to launch, and the IBO estimated an expanded citywide version would cost $425 million by 2028. Meanwhile, Mamdani's plan to establish five city-run grocery stores that sell items 30% below market value has drawn skepticism from retail analysts and economists who question whether the discounts can be sustained without ongoing taxpayer subsidies. Fox News Digital asked the mayor's office what civil service guidelines justified the early salary bumps, why raises were authorized the same day Mamdani warned of a $12 billion deficit and how City Hall reconciles the payroll increases with budget constraints on programs like universal childcare and free transit. A spokesperson for City Hall did not immediately return a request for comment. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital’s Leo Briceno contributed to this report.

articles.title: Mamdani recovering after ‘successful’ Achilles surgery
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is recovering at Gracie Mansion—the mayor’s official residence—following a “successful” surgery on his injured Achilles, which was caused by a recreational soccer game earlier this month. “Today, Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani underwent a surgical procedure to repair his Achilles tendon,” Joe Calvello, Mamdani’s press secretary, said in a statement. …
articles.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is recovering at Gracie Mansion—the mayor’s official residence—following a “successful” surgery on his injured Achilles, which was caused by a recreational soccer game earlier this month.

“Today, Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani underwent a surgical procedure to repair his Achilles tendon,” Joe Calvello, Mamdani’s press secretary, said in a statement .

Calvello confirmed that the procedure started at 11:33 a.m. EST and concluded at 12:42 p.m. EST on Friday.

“The surgery was successful, and the Mayor is expected to make a full recovery,” the press secretary continued. “He was discharged from the hospital and is now resting comfortably at Gracie Mansion.”

“We are extremely grateful for the first-class care the Mayor received from the medical staff today. First Deputy Mayor Dean Fuleihan is leading day-to-day operations today,” he concluded.

Mamdani first appeared injured last week at a morning press conference where he disclosed his injury. The mayor injured his Achilles while playing a soccer game against New York City’s press corps.

He said he forgot the stretch before hitting the field, telling reporters, “I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch, and I forgot that I was 35 and soon after I tore my Achilles.”

“I will be in a boot for six to eight weeks. I will play soccer in about nine months,” Mamdani added.

Due to the surgery, he will also not be able to attend the rescheduled Macy’s Thanksgiving parade. He remarked that he was scared to have surgery, saying it was his first procedure.

“I’ve been looking forward to attending this parade, and now, as a result of the rescheduling, I will not be able to make it because of the doctor’s orders,” the mayor stated.

Macy’s pushed its Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday, citing a severe storm moving up the East Coast, which is forecast to bring heavy rain and wind. The parade is now scheduled for 8:30 a.m. EST Saturday.

articles.title: Dean says ‘Pennsylvania deserves better’ as she mulls challenging Fetterman
articles.summary: Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.) said she believed “Pennsylvania deserves better” amid speculation that she may launch a Senate bid in 2028 for Sen. John Fetterman’s (D-Pa.) seat. She stated Sunday on NBC’s “Meet the Press” that she was taking her time to “seriously consider” the possibility of running. “I’ve known John a long time, and…
articles.body:
Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.) said she believed “Pennsylvania deserves better” amid speculation that she may launch a Senate bid in 2028 for Sen. John Fetterman’s (D-Pa.) seat.

She stated Sunday on NBC’s “ Meet the Press ” that she was taking her time to “seriously consider” the possibility of running.

“I’ve known John a long time, and sadly, I see he has moved away from the values that got him elected. Pennsylvania deserves better,” Dean continued. “I don’t have a time frame. I have to tell you, over the holidays, I’m going to spend a lot of time eating and speaking with my close family members, my kids and my grandkids, my daughters-in-law, and so I’ll take my time.”

The lawmaker previously criticized Fetterman for his video appearance in September at the GOP’s midterm convention in Dallas, where he introduced Sen. Dave McCormick (R-Pa.) as a “great friend.”

“I will tell you from the ground from suburban Philadelphia, my constituents are livid,” Dean told reporters at a House Democratic event shortly after the convention. “Those who went out and knocked doors for him — they are absolutely livid.”

Progressive Democrats sharply criticized Fetterman over his split with the party on high-profile votes, including voting against an Iran war powers resolution that attempted to scale down U.S. military action.

Fetterman’s staunch backing of Israel has also drawn some eyes within the caucus as he has repeatedly asserted he would leave the Democratic Party during his Senate term if it turned its back on Israel or if Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) is elected as Senate majority leader .

The Pennsylvania Democrat said he was still “ considering things ” regarding a possible re-election bid in 2028, but challengers have already begun to announce their candidacies. Ahmed Moor, a Palestinian American writer and businessperson from Philadelphia, became the first Democrat to formally launch a 2028 challenge against Fetterman.

Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.) indicated she would back incumbent Democrats seeking re-election in 2028, including Fetterman. She stated she would assume Fetterman would run for another term until he announced other plans.

“So far, we assume he is. And we are going to win Pennsylvania,” she added.
